name: Bob Roberts
role: Medora freighter, saloon keeper and Deadwood route pioneer
bio: Bob Roberts was a Medora freighter and saloon keeper. In the spring of 1884 the paper reported him running mule freight outfits between Medora and Deadwood, leading the first train over the new route and cutting a shorter road to the Black Hills. That fall he served as one of Dakota's deputy commissioners for the New Orleans exposition, travelled to Bismarck on its business, and planned to start for New Orleans with Vic Smith in January 1885; late that month he left instead for Wales to settle his father's estate. The Cow Boy also noted his cellar for liquor stock, his building (where Sam Whitney set up house in April 1885), and a pet bear that amused the town. In January 1886 the firm of Roberts & Co., his partnership with James Hannigan, was dissolved, and that July his lease of a building to Billings County for county purposes was signed and filed.
